Global Acquisitions U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE

JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION SECTION 1: IDENTIFICATION OF THE AGENCY AND THE CONTRACTING ACTIVITY

Department of State Contracting Activity [X] Acquisitions Management [ ] Foreign Service Institute [ ] Office of Foreign Missions [ ] U.S. Mission to the United Nations [ ] Overseas Post Requiring Activity The Bureau of Personnel and Training, Talent Acquisitions, Board of Examiners (PERT/BEX) - Foreign Service Test Development

SECTION 2: NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING APPROVED

Approval is requested to solicit and award, on a sole-source basis, a bridge contract to the incumbent contractor, HUMAN RESOURCES RESEARCH ORGANIZATION (HUMRRO), located at 66 Canal Center Plaza, Suite 700, Alexandria, VA 22314-1578, to provide continued test development and administration services described in Section 3 on behalf of the Requiring Activity.

The existing contract was modified through Modification P00033 on November 11, 2025, extending the period of performance through May 31, 2026, in the amount of █████████. Accordingly, May 31, 2026, is the final date on which authority may be exercised under the current contract.

This bridge action will ensure uninterrupted mission support while the Government completes a full and open competition for the follow-on requirement. The anticipated contract type is hybrid firm-fixed-price with other direct costs for travel.

SECTION 3: DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES/SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY’S NEEDS

The contractor shall provide continuous development, administration, maintenance, evaluation, refinement, and validation of legally and professionally validated written examinations used as the initial screening tool in the selection of qualified candidates for Foreign Service employment, including Foreign Service Officers and Foreign Service Specialists.

These services are mission-critical and directly support the requirements of the Foreign Service Act of 1980, as amended, which authorizes the Secretary of State to prescribe written and other examinations for appointment to the U.S. Foreign Service. This acquisition supports the delivery of secure computer-based testing instruments essential to identifying qualified candidates for diplomatic service worldwide.

Any lapse in services would result in: • Disruption of scheduled Foreign Service testing and assessment cycles • Delays in recruiting and processing qualified candidates for critical positions • Adverse impacts to staffing pipelines for diplomatic, security, and technical roles • Reduced mission readiness affecting worldwide diplomatic operations ██████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████

SECTION 4: IDENTIFICATION OF THE STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION

This acquisition is conducted under the authority of 41 USC 3304, as implemented by FAR 6.103 and substantiated by the following:

☒ FAR 6.103-2 – Unusual and Compelling Urgency.

SECTION 5: DEMONSTRATION THAT THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR’S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR THE NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED

The incumbent contractor, HUMAN RESOURCES RESEARCH ORGANIZATION (HumRRO), is uniquely qualified to provide the required services during the bridge period for the following reasons:

1. HumRRO possesses extensive specialized expertise in Foreign Service testing, including development and maintenance of the Department of State’s selection systems for the Foreign Service Officer Test (FSOT), Foreign Service Oral Assessment (FSOA), Consular Fellows Program Test (CFPT), Office Management Specialist Test (OMST), Foreign Service Specialist Assessment System (FSSAS), Diplomatic Technology Officer Test (DTOT), and Diplomatic Security assessments.

2. ████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████ ███████████████████

3. The incumbent ensures compliance with all applicable professional and regulatory standards, including the Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures (29 CFR § 1607), the Principles for the Validation and Use of Personnel Selection Procedures, the Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing, and Section 508 accessibility requirements.

4. HumRRO has demonstrated exceptional performance under the current contract, consistently providing high-quality testing services, effective project management, flexibility in supporting evolving requirements, and reliable administration support.

5. The incumbent provides critical continuity through established coordination with the Board of Examiners (BEX), ongoing assessor training support, recurring program reporting, and litigation support related to testing and validation activities.

6. Transitioning to a new contractor during the bridge period would create significant operational and security risks, including disruption to testing schedules, loss of continuity in candidate assessment processes, potential compromise of test security, and delays associated with recreating or transferring psychometric and validation data essential to the program.

7. Immediate continuity of services is required to prevent a lapse in mission-critical support. No other source could reasonably assume performance within the required timeframe without substantial disruption to Foreign Service hiring operations.

Accordingly, only the incumbent contractor can satisfy the Government’s urgent requirement during the bridge period.

SECTION 6. DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS WERE SOLICITED FROM AS

MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS IS PRACTICABLE, INCLUDING WHETHER A NOTICE WAS OR

WILL BE PUBLICIZED AS REQUIRED BY FAR SUBPART 5.2 AND, IF NOT, WHICH EXCEPTION

UNDER FAR 5.201 APPLIES

This bridge action is limited in duration and scope and is intended solely to maintain continuity of services while the competitive follow-on acquisition is completed.

The Government is actively pursuing a full and open competition for the permanent requirement, including development of the acquisition strategy, market research, and preparation of the solicitation documentation.

This bridge contract does not replace or delay competition but enables it.

SECTION 7. DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED COST TO THE GOVERNMENT IS FAIR AND REASONABLE

SECTION 8. DESCRIPTION OF THE MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED (SEE PART 10) AND THE

RESULTS OR A STATEMENT OF THE REASON MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED

Market research for the long-term requirement has been conducted/is ongoing in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Parts 10 (Market Research). While other potential sources are expected to compete for the follow-on contract, no one can assume performance within the limited timeframe required for this bridge action without unacceptable risk to mission continuity.

SECTION 9. ANY OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING THE USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN

COMPETITION

The original contract was competed when originally solicited. Failure to award this bridge contract would result in:

• Interruption of critical services • Potential degradation of mission performance • Increased cost and risk associated with emergency acquisition actions • Loss of operational continuity The bridge period will be kept to the minimum duration necessary to complete the competitive procurement.

SECTION 10. LISTING OF THE SOURCES, IF ANY, THAT EXPRESSED, IN WRITING, AN INTEREST IN THE ACQUISITION A Request for Information (RFI) was posted on SAM.gov to acquire a list of potentially capable contractors for Foreign Service Officer Test (FSOT) services against 19AQMM-26-RFI-1002. The Program Office (PO) was asked to review the capability statements from the market research results to further narrow the number of sources to the highest qualified companies that can meet their requirements. Through analysis of the PO’s review, the CO has determined to solicit the requirement under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 611710 - Educational Support Services. ████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████ ██████████████████████ ██████████████████████████████ ████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████ ██████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████ █████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████ ███████████████████████████████████████ SECTION 11. STATEMENT OF THE ACTIONS, IF ANY, THE AGENCY MAY TAKE TO REMOVE OR

OVERCOME ANY BARRIERS TO COMPETITION BEFORE ANY SUBSEQUENT ACQUISITION FOR THE SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED

The Government is taking the following actions to ensure full and open competition for the follow-on requirement:

• Finalizing acquisition planning and strategy • Completing market research • Preparing a competitive solicitation • Establishing realistic timeliness to prevent future bridge actions The bridge contract is a one-time, limited action to support competition and not replace it.

The estimated date of the new contract award for the recompete acquisition is May 31, 2027.
